title: Eleven Seconds and One Bend
subtitle: 事故与安全 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 事故与安全（灾害防范·安全与预防）
meta: 主题语境：事故与安全（灾害防范·安全与预防）　|　核心词汇：crash　|　正文 335 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 crash 的含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1963 my uncle ① walked away from a crash on a bend that had taken eleven others, and he said the walking away was the whole of the luck. The ② crash, meaning the collision and not the noise, lasted eleven seconds and stayed that short; crash, he said, is the only thing on a road that is judged by how little of it is remembered.

Every ③ crash on that bend had the same witness, and the ④ crash at the end, meaning the one he kept from my grandmother and not either of those, was the only one anybody ever reported twice. Crash, my aunt said, is nine parts witness and one part somebody willing to report; my uncle said the reporting is the part that fills eleven seconds.

My father meant the other thing entirely: he said ⑤ the crash was the whole of the market, meaning the collapse and not the collision. The ⑥ crash, meaning the collapse and not any of that, is the only thing in a market that everybody predicts afterwards and nobody prevents; crash, he said, is either something you walk away from or the only word that means both a collision and a collapse. She said the collapse is the part they remember.

By 1971 the ⑦ crash had become a line in an insurance form, and the form had become an argument about the witness. The ⑧ crash of the whole thing, my uncle wrote in October, was one bend and thirty years of reporting; crash, he said, is either the one at the end or the reason you learned to report. He said the reporting was never mentioned.

The ⑨ crash I remember is the one at the end, which happened in 1977 and is still described as the quietest in the county. A ⑩ crash, my aunt said in 1979, is the only thing that improves by being reported; every crash, she said, is a collapse that has agreed to look like a collision. She said the collapse was the honest half.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请将对应义项填入表中。
options: B. n. 碰撞（指那次相撞本身，与那声巨响相对）
C. 固定搭配：walk away from a crash 从一场车祸中安然脱身
D. n. 车祸（指那个弯道上的每一次）
E. n. 车祸（指末尾那一次）
F. n. 崩溃；暴跌（指市场崩盘）
G. n. 车祸（指保险单上提到的那一次）
H. n. 撞击；坠毁（抽象总称）

items.q: walked away from a crash on a bend that had taken eleven others
The crash, meaning the collision and not the noise
the crash was the whole of the market
the crash had become a line in an insurance form
The crash of the whole thing
A crash, my aunt said in 1979

answers.why: walk away from a crash 意为“从一场车祸中安然脱身”，1963 年叔叔在一个已经夺走另外十一人的弯道上的车祸里安然脱身。
crash 意为“碰撞”，指那次相撞本身而不是那声巨响，只持续了十一秒。
crash 指那个弯道上每一次车祸，每一次都有同一个目击者。
crash 指末尾那一次（他对祖母隐瞒的那一次），是唯一有人报过两次的。
crash 意为“崩溃、暴跌”，父亲说崩盘就是那个市场的全部，指的是市场崩盘而不是那次碰撞。
crash 为经济用法，指市场崩盘而不是那次碰撞，是市场里人人事后都能预见、却无人阻止的东西。
crash 意为“车祸”，指保险单上提到的那一次，到 1971 年这次车祸成了保险单上的一行。
crash 意为“撞击、坠毁”，叔叔十月写道，整件事的撞击是一个弯道三十年的报案。
crash 意为“撞车、碰撞”，我记得的是末尾那一次，1977 年发生，至今仍被说成全县最安静的。
crash 为抽象总称，姑姑说一场车祸是唯一会因为被报案而变好的东西。

那次碰撞，指的是那次相撞本身而不是那声巨响，只持续了十一秒，并且一直是那么短。（crash）
那个弯道上每一次车祸都有同一个目击者。（crash）
末尾那一次车祸，指的是他对祖母隐瞒的那一次，是唯一有人报过两次的。（crash）
父亲说崩盘就是那个市场的全部，指的是市场崩盘而不是那次碰撞。（crash）
1979 年姑姑说，一场车祸是唯一会因为被报案而变好的东西。（crash）

The crash, meaning the collision and not the noise, lasted eleven seconds and stayed that short.
Every crash on that bend had the same witness.
The crash at the end, meaning the one he kept from my grandmother and not either of those, was the only one anybody ever reported twice.
My father said the crash was the whole of the market, meaning the collapse and not the collision.
A crash, my aunt said in 1979, is the only thing that improves by being reported.
